symptom: The v353 static negative-catalog guard pinned 18 cases, per-case fields and global policy text but accepted arbitrary new top-level fields. A catalog with positiveControlsVerified=true, executionReady=true or a caller-controlled independentTestTrustRoot object could still pass the static catalog test despite introducing unsupported authority-looking metadata. This was a specification-integrity gap only; no independent verifier, trusted evidence, scoring or production path ran.
lesson: Exact denial codes and global custody statements do not prevent unsupported authority-like metadata from being added at the catalog root. A future consumer could mistakenly interpret such fields as an independently verified positive control or an execution gate.
guardrail: Close the catalog root to an independently pinned exact key set, in addition to the existing per-case field and policy checks. Mutation-test added positiveControlsVerified, executionReady and independentTestTrustRoot fields. Do not treat a static catalog PASS as an executed verifier, positive attestation, scoring authorization or production authority.
